                        Profile of F. A. Ahmed College, Garoimari

            The year 1984 of the last century was an eventful year and epoch in the history of Garoimari and
    its neighboring areas. At that time, a handful of people got knowledge literacy, the logic of higher
    education, by and large, disappeared in the area. It was almost beyond the dream of generating higher
    educated people from a man-power producing industry establishing in Garoimari. A few among all could
    realize the need of higher education. Among them, we must to take the name of the following
    personalities like Omor Ali Sarkar (the founder president of Managing Committee), AbdulHakim (the
    founder secretary), many others who endeavored their relentless effort in establishing the college. Abdul
    Qayyum Al Aman took pioneer responsibility as Honorary Principal of the college when regular classes
    started. He played an active and pioneering role in shaping and moulding the foundation of the college.
    Besides, the contributions of all the MLAs of Chhaygaon Constituency since 1980 till date aren’t less
    memorable for their all kind of assistance. Garoimari is mostly dominated by the minority Muslims
    people dependent basically on agrarian economy, the people of the area extended spontaneous support to
    establish a college. The mission of the college was to spread the ray of the higher education by breaking
    the barrier of darkness among the rural people.
            In the year 1984 on an auspicious day, the dream turns into reality with the establishment of the
    higher educational institution named F.A.Ahmed College. The college is named in memory of
    Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed, an Assamese son who decorated the sovereign chair of India during the period,
    1974 to 1977. It is the only higher educational institution that has been imparting education in the Degree
    Classes (Arts) since its inception.
            At the initial stage, Abdur Rahman Khan was the honorary principal of the college. Mr. Habibur
    Rahman renderedhis service as Principal of the college to till his retirement on 31st December 2014. The
    college was provincialized by the State Government of Assam w.e.f. 01/01/2013 but the Post of the
    principal was not provincialized. It always will remain in-compensatory to him who offers about 24
    year’s prolonged service. After his departure, Abdul AwalSahab has taken the charge of the principal and
    being continuing.
            The college has its vast and sprawling campus covering area 3.34 hectares (25 bighas) of the land
    and the serene atmosphere of the college attracts one and all. The co-educational Arts Degree College
    which had a humble beginning with 161 students and 10 faculties at the time of its establishment. At
    present, about 766 number of students has been enrolled and facilitated for higher education. The teaching
    component comprises 30 faculties and various supporting services including an ‘Internal Quality
    Assurance Cell’ (IQAC). The student feedback system has been introduced to remove the deficiencies of
    the            course           and          enhancement              of          teaching           quality.
       The college has traversed a long distance since its inception. It has produced a large number of brilliant
    students into university and many of them are well placed in social as well as personal life.

                                            Credit Framework
                     Four-Year Undergraduate Programme (FYUGP)

            Each semester of a 4-Year Bachelor Degree (FYUGP) course will have a maximum of 22 credits
    with a total of 132 credits for 3-Year Degree Course and 176 credits for a 4-Year Degree Course.
    Apparently, the Masters Course will have 44 credits in a year with a total of 88 credits in two years. The
    baseline for total credits is 120 for a 3-Year course and 160 for a 4-Year course. So, a student can choose
    to have a total credit between 120 and 132 by the end of a 3-Year Bachelor Degree course.
    The basic division of credits for a 3-Year Bachelor Degree course is shown in figure alongside. The basic
    division for a 4-Year course is shown in figure. In the 4th year, there are however two options – (a)
    Degree with Honours and (b) Degree with Honours and Research. Overall, a 3-Year Degree course
    consists of two sections — a Core Section and a Common Section. While the Core Section consists of
    Major and Minor papers, the Common Section is divided into 5 sub-groups.
     Multi-disciplinary Courses
        These are 3-credit courses spanning over five different groups of subjects — (i) Natural and Physics
        Science, (ii) Mathematics, Statistics, and Computer Applications, (iii) Library, Information, and
        Media Sciences, (iv) Commerce and Management, and (v) Humanities and Social Sciences. The level
        of these courses is of Class XII.

       Ability Enhancement Courses (AEC)
        This is a 8-credit course covering Modern Indian Languages (MIL) and English Usage
        (Communication)
       Skill Enhancement Courses (SEC)
        These are various skill courses with total credit allocation of 9. In our structure, we shall have four
        skill courses starting from Semester III.
       Value-based Courses (VAC)
        The VAC courses will come from four sub groups — (i) Understanding India, (ii) Environmental
        Science, (iii) Digital and Technological Solutions, and (iv) Health & Wellness, Yoga Education,
        Sports, and Fitness. All together they will have a credit allocation of 6.
       Internship
        All students are to carry out an internship with a credit allocation of 4.

        As shown in the figures, the base credit score for a 3-Year course is 120 and a student needs to have at
    least 50% of 120 i.e. 60 credits in a subject to qualify for a major in that subject. In the same way a minor
    course will have 12 credits and a student can have two minors with a total of 24 credits. Apart from the
    Major subject, if a student can obtain 48 credits in a particular subject, the student will get a double
    major.

                        College Discipline-General Regulations

     1. Students must come to the college invariably in prescribed uniform. They must bring Identity Card and
        Student's Handbook and produce the same when asked for. This rule is considered as minimum in
        maintaining disciple of the college.
     2. All the students should read the Notice Board of the College regularly and note own important
        instructions in the Student’s Handbook.
     3. Students should be decent, courteous and polite at all times whether they are in the class or in the
        college premises.
     4. Students should respect the beauty and cleanliness of the college and take utmost care to promote the
        same.
     5. Scribbling on books, desks and walls is strictly prohibited and liable to fines.
     6. Spitting, writing and sticking anything on the college walls/rooms are strictly prohibited.
     7. Students should park their vehicles in the area allotted for the purpose,
     8. Disobedience and misbehavior towards staff members or repeated breaking of college rules or behavior
        objectionable to the good tone of the school, even outside the college premises will deserve severe
        punishment or even dismissal if warnings are ignored.
     9. Students are prohibited to go out of college premises during college hours without the permission of
        the principal. They areadvised to utilize their leisure time in the college library/ common room/
        canteen. They will not be allowed to loiter or sit in the veranda.
     10. Ragging in any form, inside or outside the campus, is strictly prohibited by law. Any student found
        indulging in ragging will be rusticated from the college.
     11. The college is a No smoking/ No Tobacco/ No Drugs/ No Alcohol Zone. Students found violating
        these rules will be dealt with as per rules of the college.
     12. Students should not damage the property of the institution. Cost of any damage will be recovered
        from the students as compensation.
     13. Students will not include in any anti-social activities or activities causing hindrance to the academic
        and administrative functioning of the college. Those found indulging in such activities will face
        disciplinary action to the extent of expulsion from the college.
     14. During the teaching hours all areas around the classrooms will be observed as Silent zones. The
        authority will deal with students who create any disturbance, as it deem right. Keep silence when the
        classes are on.
     15. Mobile phones are strictly prohibited during class and examination hours. Any violation is subject to
        severe disciplinary action.


12
      16. No student shall intentionally or recklessly disrupt or impede or attempt to disrupt or impede the
        activities and functions of the college, or any part thereof.
     17. Irregular attendance, constant negligence of assignments will be severely dealt with. A minimum
        attendance of 75% is essential for appearing in the university examinations. In case of absence due to
        unavoidable circumstances, prior permission from the appropriate authority has to be taken and
        endorsed the same handbook, In case of sickness; students will have to produce a Medical Certificate

     18. Class-tests, Unit-tests, Assignments and Terminal/Sessional examinations are obligatory on all

     19. No candidate shall make use of any unfair means in any examination.
     20. Students’ participation and active co-operation in all observation days and other co-curricular
        activities is must.

                                 College Rules and Regulations

     1.  Use of Mobile Phones by students in the College premises is restricted. Violation of this rule
         will invite severe disciplinary action.
     2. The College lays great emphasis on discipline and character building of the students. Students are
         always expected to maintain a high standard of discipline.
     3. Every student must abide by the rules and regulations of the college and the hostels. A declaration to
         that effect will have to be signed by a student at the time of admission.
     4. A student found guilty of misconduct or violating college rules shall be subject to disciplinary action.
         Disciplinary action includes expulsion from college, suspension for a period, debarring from
         appearing in examination, compulsory transfer etc.
     5. Ragging in any form is strictly prohibited in the college and hostel campus. Students found indulging
         in act of ragging shall be strongly dealt with as per the directives of Supreme Court of India.
     6. Smoking, chewing of tobacco and use of any intoxicants in the college and hostel campus is strictly
         prohibited.
     7. Loitering in the College campus or verandah is prohibited. A student may be reprimanded if found
         doing so.
     8. Cleanliness is a collective responsibility of each and every member of the College. Spitting on walls
         is strictly prohibited. Writing slogans or sticking of bills on the walls is also strictly prohibited.
     9. Students should go through the College Notice Board regularly for all information.
     10. All powers of maintenance of discipline and observance of college rules and regulations rest with the
         Principal of the College and his/her decision shall be final in all such matters.

     9. Holding of any meeting in the college or hostel premises or college playground without permission or
        against the order of the Principal.
     10. Loitering in the College campus or in the College verandah.
     11. Use of unfair means in College examinations.



                             IDENTITY CARD AND RECORD BOOK
             An identity card will be issued to every student on once the admission process of the College is
     over. The card shall contain information of the holder along with a recent passport size photograph of the
     student duly endorsed by the Principal. The Identity Card is non-transferable. A student must keep the
     Identity Card with him/her and he/she must produce the same whenever asked for. Students must renew
     his/ her Identity Card at the end of each academic year positively. Every student will be issued a
     Record Book and the same has to be properly maintained by him/her. The Record Book will be
     necessary for various official purposes concerning the student. If lost, duplicate identity card, record book
     or receipt will be issued on proper communication to the competent authority.



                                              EXAMINATIONS
             The College Examinations are held according to the College Academic Calendar. A student must
     appear in all the examinations conducted by the College during an academic year. The College adheres to
     the rules and regulations of Gauhati University. As such, a student’s performance is strictly monitored
     through continuous assessment in the theory and practical courses. Internal assessment is based on
     sessional examinations, home assignments, seminars, projects, group discussions, fieldtrips, class
     attendance etc. At the end of each semester a final external examination is conducted as per the schedule
     fixed by the University. The final result of a student will be based on the total marks obtained in both
     internal and external examinations. Students must secure pass marks in both internal and external
     examinations separately.

                                              Library
              The College possesses a library with sizeable number of books, few journals including text books
     of various subjects required for various academic programs. Moreover, the library avails a good number
     of reference books, a number of newspapers in Assamese and English. Apart from the study materials,
     our College also provides free wi-fi internet facilities to the students and staff for academic purpose.
              In our College, the students should observe the following rules and regulations in using the
     library:
         1. Library membership is compulsory for all the students’.
         2. Each student can borrow two books at a time.
         3. Students should examine the book(s) issued to him/her before leaving the library. If any damage
              or mutilation is noticed, it should be reported to the Librarian immediately. Otherwise, he/she will
              be responsible for it.

        5. Those who fail to return the borrowed books on time are subject to a fine of 50 paisa per day per
            book.
        6. If the books found damaged in any form or lost during the said period of his/her possession, the
            student will have to pay the value of the book/books as directed by the College librarian.
        7. If the library card is lost by any student it should be reported to the Librarian immediately.

                                                 ANTI-RAGGING
         In exercise of the powers conferred by clause (g) of sub section 1 of section 26 of the UGC Act, 1956
     the UGC hereby makes the regulations, namely : “UGC Regulations on Curbing the Menace of Ragging
     in Higher Educational Institutions, 2009”, our College has decided to implement fully the anti-ragging
     regulations of the UGC.

     (A) What Constitutes Ragging:
         Ragging constitutes one or more of any of the following act
         a) Any conduct by any student or students whether by words spoken or written or by an act which has
            the effect of teasing, treating or handling with rudeness a fresher or any other students.
         b) Indulging in rowdy or undisciplined activities by any student or students which causes or likely to
            cause annoyance, hardship, physical or psychological harm or to raise fear or apprehension thereof
            in any fresher or any other student.
         c) Asking any student to do any act against his/ her will which has the effect of causing or generating
            a sense of shame, or torment or embarrassment so as to adversely affect the physique or psyche of
         such fresher or any other student.


18
            d) Any act by a senior student that prevents, disrupts or disturbs the regular academic activity of any
           other student or a fresher.
           e) Exploiting the services of a fresher or any other student for completing the academic tasks
           assigned to an individual or a group of students.
           f) Any act of financial extortion or forceful expenditure burden on a fresher or any other student by
           students.
           g) Any act of physical abuse including all variants of it: sexual abuse, homosexual assaults, stripping,
           forcing obscene and lewd acts, gestures, causing bodily harm or any other danger to health of person.
           h) Any act or abuse by spoken words, emails, post, public insults which would also include deriving
           perverted pleasure, vicarious or sadistic thrill from actively or passively participating in the
           discomfiture to fresher or any other students.
           i) Any acts that affect the mental health and self-confidence of a fresher or any other student with or
           without intent to derive a sadistic pleasure or showing off power, authority or superiority by a student
           over any fresher or any other student.

          (B) Administrative action in the event of ragging:
              There is an Anti-Ragging Committee and an anti-ragging squad in the College. The Anti-
              Ragging Committee shall take an appropriate action as per the provision under “UGC
              Regulations on Curbing the Menace of Ragging in Higher Educational Institutions, 2009” in
              regard to punishment student depending on the nature and gravity of the guilty established by the
              Anti-Ragging Squad. Following is the Anti-Ragging Committee in our College:
